title: HTTP semantics, smuggling, desync

atom_notes.A06: two layers resolve the same bytes to different messages, which is the definition of desync
atom_notes.A04: the front end and back end state diverge and stay diverged
atom_notes.A05: the framing itself is something the bytes can disagree about
atom_notes.A15: proxy and server configuration decides whether the class exists at all

required_cells.why: know the proxy chain and HTTP versions before sending anything malformed
desync detection needs controlled variation, not a spray
exploitation means a captured request from another user, which needs a safe proof
a control request that does not desync is mandatory, and so is a lab
impact framing that explains blast radius on shared infrastructure
retest after a proxy config change

entries.name: smuggler
entries.role: Desync detection across CL.TE, TE.CL, TE.TE and TE.TE obfuscation variants
preconditions: two layers that disagree about message framing
oracle: a request that desyncs the backend
a second response arriving on the wrong connection
entries.note: Only against infrastructure you own or a lab. A desync can corrupt other users' requests, which makes it the most dangerous class here.
entries.mirror_note: no mirror row covers this entry

entries.name: h2cSmuggler
entries.role: HTTP/2 cleartext upgrade smuggling, the class most scanners completely miss
preconditions: a front end that forwards an upgrade header
oracle: an internal request reaching a path the front end would block
detected_by: upgrade header forwarded to a backend that speaks h2c

entries.name: Framing bisection across hops
entries.role: Which hop disagrees about where a request ends. Bisection by placing a boundary marker at a chosen offset and watching which side treats it as data gives the seam without a scanner.
preconditions: a marker observable in a response body or a log
a request shape accepted by both hops
oracle: a marker that appears in the second response but was sent in the first
the offset at which the two hops stop agreeing, measured by moving the marker

entries.mirror_note: no mirror row covers this entry
entries.name: Header precedence per hop
entries.role: Which of two conflicting headers each hop believes. Sending both with distinguishable values and reading what the origin echoes back names the precedence order without guessing.
preconditions: a header the origin reflects or acts on
oracle: the value the origin acts on, matched to one of the two sent
a different value acted on by the edge, shown by a behaviour change before the origin

entries.mirror_note: no mirror row covers this entry
entries.name: Stateful transport framing: WebSocket and WebTransport
entries.role: Framing rules and per stream authorisation on transports that stay open. A socket is not subject to same origin once established, and a multiplexed stream that shares authorisation is a stream that leaks it.
preconditions: the application exposes a WebSocket or WebTransport endpoint
oracle: a frame the specification forbids accepted, such as an oversized control frame or an unmasked client frame
a cross origin socket established without an origin check
state in one stream changed by closing another, which is shared authorisation

tree.q: Are you in a lab or on shared infrastructure?
tree.why: This question comes first, before any technique. A desync can corrupt other users' in flight requests. On shared infrastructure that is not a test, it is an incident.

branches.action: stop. document the suspicion and the reason, then move to a lab. nothing else in this tree applies
